newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore paper says Cambodia ASEAN entry can wait.
newsitem.headline: Singapore paper says Cambodia ASEAN entry can wait.

text.p: Cambodia's entry into the Association of South East Nations (ASEAN) can wait, Singapore's Straits Times newspaper said in an editorial on Tuesday.
The pro-government English-language daily said "current events suggest that now is not an appropriate time" for Cambodia to join the regional grouping.

Fighting rocked the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh over the weekend, leaving Second Prime Minister Hun Sen in control of the city. Rival First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, now in France, has vowed to resist.

The situation raises questions about who is really in charge of Cambodia and could speak for it when ASEAN meets on July 23 to formalise entry of Cambodia, Burma and Laos into the group, the Straits Times said.
ASEAN "may want to consider holding back membership, not to penalise Cambodians but as an acknowledgement of the state of unrest there," the paper said.
It said eventual Cambodian entry to ASEAN is inevitable, but for now: "Evidently, Cambodia is not quite ready."

"Cambodians need more time to put their own house in order. They should know that delayed membership is a consequence of the violence in their country, and unless they end the bloodshed and fighting, there is a price to pay on the diplomatic front."
ASEAN foreign ministers have set a special meeting on Thursday in Kuala Lumpur to discuss the crisis, the Malaysian news agency Bernama reported.

The Singapore foreign ministry earlier called for an end to violence in Cambodia and said: "Singapore disapproves of the change of government through violent means and calls on all parties to adhere to the constitutional processes in place."
However, Singapore has made no official comment on the status of Cambodia's ASEAN entry.

Noting ASEAN members generally argue internal politics should not be its concern, analysts say what may be critical is whether the situation affects Cambodia's ability to meet such commitments as attending ASEAN's numerous meetings and adopting certain obligations on trade.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
